title: Realization of a finite integral lattice enlargement by a central isogeny
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $H$ be a semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial. Fix a split maximal torus $T$ and its root datum $(X,\Phi,X_*,\Phi^\vee)$ in the conventions of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Suppose that the roots span $V=X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$. Let $L\subset V$ be a free abelian subgroup of rank $\dim_{\mathbf Q}V$, with $X\subseteq L$ and $L/X$ finite, such that $\langle L,\alpha^\vee\rangle\subseteq\mathbf Z$ for every root $\alpha$. The pairing is extended rationally from $X\times X_*$. There exist a split semisimple $F$-group scheme $H_L$, a split maximal torus $T_L\subset H_L$, an identification $X^*(T_L)=L$, and a surjective homomorphism $f:H_L\to H$ with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel, carrying $T_L$ onto $T$, such that $f|_{T_L}^*:X\to L$ is the specified inclusion. Moreover $f$ is an isomorphism if and only if $L=X$. Finite kernel means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and central means commuting with all group elements after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. No restriction on the characteristic or on the order of $L/X$ is imposed.

source.place: Appendix C.35, printed p.615; Theorem 23.55 and Corollary 23.56, printed p.501; Theorem 23.9, printed p.487; Proposition 23.5, printed pp.485--486, centrality and isomorphism criteria.

proof.text: Put $L^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(L,\mathbf Z)$. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, its rational coroot restricts to $c_\alpha\in L^\vee$ by hypothesis. The reduced root datum of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] gives $\langle\alpha,c_\alpha\rangle=2$ and $s_\alpha(\Phi)=\Phi$. For $l\in L$, $s_\alpha(l)=l-\langle l,c_\alpha\rangle\alpha\in L$ since $\alpha\in X\subset L$; $s_\alpha^2=1$. The generated reflection group acts faithfully on the finite set $\Phi$, because $\Phi$ spans $V=L\otimes\mathbf Q$, so it is finite. Distinct coroots remain distinct on $L$, since they are already distinct on $X$. Reducedness is unchanged in $V$. Thus these data satisfy all the reduced-root-datum axioms of the realization theorem.

source.place: Appendix C.28 and C.35, printed pp.613--615: verify the axioms on the enlarged lattice.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-realization] to obtain $(H_L,T_L)$ with character lattice $L$, roots $\Phi$ and coroots $c_\alpha$. The roots still span $L\otimes\mathbf Q=V$. Consequently [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span], applied to this split reductive group, makes $H_L$ semisimple.

source.place: Theorem 23.55, p.501, followed by Proposition 21.48, p.439.

proof.text: For the inclusion $u:X\hookrightarrow L$, take the root bijection to be the identity and every root exponent to be $1$. Then $u(\alpha)=\alpha$ and $u^\vee(c_\alpha)=\alpha^\vee$, the latter because restriction back to $X$ recovers the original functional. The map is injective with finite cokernel by hypothesis. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization] with source group $H_L$ and target $H$. That theorem gives $f:H_L\to H$, surjective with finite kernel, carrying $T_L$ onto $T$, with the specified pullback $u$. Its centrality criterion applies since every exponent is $1$. Its isomorphism criterion says $f$ is an isomorphism exactly when $u$ is an isomorphism; for this inclusion that is equivalent to $L=X$. No separability condition is invoked.
